'''Daniel Gafford''' (born October 1, 1998) is an American college [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC).

==High school career==
Gafford was a four star recruit in high school, and received offers in 2015 from several schools, including [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]]. On August 1, 2015, Gafford committed to [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Arkansas Basketball Recruiting: Daniel Gafford Commits to the Razorbacks|author=Harper, Doc|url=https://www.arkansasfight.com/2015/8/1/9085589/arkansas-basketball-recruiting-daniel-gafford-commits-razorbacks|date=August 1, 2015|accessdate=June 21, 2018|work=Arkansas Fight}}</ref> Gafford also played football growing up and was a wide receiver until ninth grade at [[El Dorado High School (Arkansas)|El Dorado High School]] (pronounced El Doe-Ray-Doe). He also was in the marching band and credits that to the development of his skill set.<ref>{{cite news |title=High-flying Daniel Gafford a force for surging Arkansas |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/12/22/high-flying-daniel-gafford-a-force-for-surging-arkansas/108858280/ |accessdate=June 22, 2018 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=December 22, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
In his first start for the Razorbacks, Gafford finished a perfect 8 for 8 shooting, along with 7 rebounds and 6 blocks against [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Gafford shines in first start|author=Hutchinson, Andrew|website=247Sports|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Daniel-Gafford-shines-in-first-start-Arkansas-Razorbacks-beat-Minnesota-Golden-Gophers-95-79-112058150/|date=December 9, 2017|accessdate=June 21, 2018}}</ref> Gafford posted 21 points, 10 rebounds and seven blocks against No. 14 [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stone |first1=Chris |title=NBA Draft watch: Arkansas' Daniel Gafford has potential to thrive as traditional big man |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/news/daniel-gafford-arkansas-nba-draft-2018-mock-highlights-stats-scouting-report-wingspan/4cya8wpo3onq110lpforvc19c |accessdate=June 22, 2018 |work=[[Sporting News]] |date=March 2, 2018}}</ref> After a freshman season where he averaged 11.8 points 6.2 rebounds per game, Gafford announced that he would return to Arkansas for his sophomore year rather than declare for the [[2018 NBA Draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Daniel Gafford to return to Arkansas rather than head to NBA|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22923623/daniel-gafford-return-sophomore-season-arkansas|date=March 26, 2018|accessdate=June 21, 2018|work=espn}}</ref> After his freshman season, Gafford was named to the SEC All-Freshman team.<ref>{{cite web|title=3 Hogs honored by SEC coaches|author=Hutchinson, Andrew|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Bolt/3-Arkansas-Razorbacks-honored-named-to-coaches-All-SEC-teams-Jaylen-Barford-Daryl-Macon-Daniel-Gafford-115898207/|date=March 6, 2018|work=247 Sports|accessdate=June 21, 2018}}</ref> On March 18, 2019, after Gafford's sophomore season, it was announced that Gafford would skip the [[2019 National Invitation Tournament]] to prepare for the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Arkansas star Daniel Gafford, projected first-round pick, skipping NIT to prepare for NBA Draft|author=Boone, Kyle|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/arkansas-star-daniel-gafford-projected-first-round-pick-skipping-nit-to-prepare-for-nba-draft/|date=March 18, 2019|work=[[CBS Sports]]|accessdate=March 18, 2019}}</ref> Gafford improved his statistics during his second year at Arkansas, averaging 16.9 points, 8.6 rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game. He was named to the 2019 SEC All-Defensive Team, as well as a 1st Team All-SEC pick. Gafford was known for his thunderous dunks, especially alley-oops, and his shot blocking ability. He was a crowd favorite during Razorback home games at [[Bud Walton Arena]].
